title: Welsh-Powell 4-coloring for adjacency-aware palette
description:
Replace the current 'pid % 20 palette-wrap' coloring in PatchRenderer with a Welsh-Powell greedy graph coloring over the patch-adjacency graph, so neighboring patches always get different colors.

Current behavior: PatchRenderer.buildFaceColors picks PALETTE[pid % 20]. With 82 patches on the skull, colors wrap ~4x so adjacent same-color patches visually merge — the human viewer sees one blob where there are actually 4-5 distinct patches.

New behavior:
1. Build a patch-adjacency graph from the face-adjacency graph already computed in SemanticPatchDecomposer.
2. Order patches by descending degree (Welsh-Powell).
3. For each patch in that order, pick the lowest-index color not used by any already-colored neighbor.
4. By the four-color theorem, planar patch arrangements are always 4-colorable; in practice 4-6 colors suffice even on high-patch-count meshes.
5. Keep the existing 20-color palette as the source pool — pick 4-6 visually distinct colors from it, assign in Welsh-Powell order.

Expected outcome on the skull: no more visual merging of adjacent same-colored patches; every patch boundary is a visible color change in the render.

Originated from PATCH-1+2 follow-up discussion.
definition-of-done: PatchRenderer switched to Welsh-Powell coloring fed by patch-adjacency from SemanticPatchDecomposer (or a new decomposer output field for patch adjacency). Skull multiview visibly shows no two touching patches sharing a color.
testing-plan: uv run label-patches /tmp/skull.obj --force and visually inspect the multiview — every patch boundary is a color transition.
